questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic level and the options to travel in the area close by. I had never been to the US prior to my exchange and had always wanted to go.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had a friend who had been there year prior to myself, which helped me a lot. I found it a bit hard to find information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a 3-day orientation programme. It was not specifically for exchange students but gave a fine introduction of campus and the neighborhood, as well practical stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation was not really socially oriented- I would have loved to have gotten to know more students early.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found a room through AirBnB - I worked out quite well for me and I was happy about it.

I lived 3km away from campus, which took me 20minutes by bus/bike

I really liked to live off campus and it gave me some great options to get to see more of Berkeley

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
The bus is free for UC students and public transport in the Bay area is generally very well connected compared to other cities in California.

Most students live just by campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The latter rating is rather an indication of the general housing options. My own was 5/5, but you have to put in some work to find a good option

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process is very extensive, however definitely worth it

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I applied through mobility in the fall 2023

I applied through UC to a specific UC institution in the early summer 2024. I wrote a long application, did a language test (duolingo is the cheapest), got recommendations from my professors

Got confirmation on my spot at Berkeley august 2024 and started the process to apply for a visa. This takes quite while, however not due to UC but rather the US immigration system...

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My host institution held a meeting about the process for the UC application process and did a presentation about the different UC institutions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got all the classes I wanted, but just barely. 

I could only register for two courses within my own major in the first registration phase, but got the two other courses I wanted in the Add/drop period which runs for the first 2 weeks of the semester

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It is extensive, but worth every stressfull moment. Take it easy and dont worry to much about all the deadlines for documents, you'll be fine.

Be aware that you need to write the professors if you want to enroll in their graduate courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
High level - However as a University of Copenhagen student you are well off.

The workload was distributed throughout the semester in another than I am used to UCPH

The workload was high just up until midterms (just before spring break), but really eased out afterwards. 

Checkout the sites Berkeleytime, they have student evalutations and grade distribution on most courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took 4 classes all within my own major Economics, the first three were uper division courses and the last one was graduate level

I can recommend all if you're interested in Public/Labor and have ambitions of doing research- However be aware that 13units is full time studies

ECON 148 - Data science for Economist (4 units)
-Cool course you learn to code and do data analysis in python 
-A bit extensive if you have no prior coding experience as I did
-The course I used most time on probably

ECON 152 - Wage theory and public policy(4 units)
-Labor economics, got introduced to some interesting economic model and stylized facts about the labor market as well as some research 
-Pretty easy compared to the other courses, had weekly assignments, a midterm, an final all counted 1/3 of final grade

ECON 191 - Topics in Economic Research (seminar) (4 units)
-You have to write a paper in the same length as a bachelors thesis a bit more extensive than I had thought

ECON 230B - Public Economics (Graduate) (4 units)
-Great professors
-Only one weekly class of 2 hours and three assignments throughout the semester. 
-Follows same setup as courses on UCPH, but without dicussion sections

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More or less the same- It is a bit more formal in the communication, but you have the option to attend office hours and speak to the professors in person.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Have done allready

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Can really recommend ECON230B

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a bit more difficult than I thought, but you'll get along

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I regret not joining a sports club when I got there

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not being as open as the Americans are

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Travel

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go go go! I would have loved to stay for longer

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Getting to know myself better
Learning about the American culture and people
Going places I've always wanted to

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being a lot alone, and having to seek options and make a living on your own.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
